clue.text: Scoffed at Judge? One gets sack

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to hit the sack is to go to bed, so sack can mean bed

explanation.surface: A judge is mocked; meanwhile someone gets fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge?' looks like part of the definition, but it only supplies J.
explanation.definitionFit: Jibed is a synonym of jeered or mocked, so scoffed at fits as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: First person in France to grasp passable quip

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so the French pronoun wraps the other piece

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person pronoun
OK means acceptable or passable

explanation.surface: A French speaker is the first to understand a mediocre gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty remark, a near synonym for a jest.

clue.text: Warning not entirely accepted in trade: a sign of things to come?

definitions.text: a sign of things to come?

indicators.note: something accepted in a group is taken inside it, so the shortened warning goes within the trade word

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word for warning is dropped

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: A trader half-heeds a warning, wondering if it foretells the future.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: the instrument foretells weather rather than events, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling or rising glass forecasts the weather, so the instrument is a playful sign of things to come.

clue.text: Adrenaline unexpectedly surrounding one European Parliament

indicators.note: surrounding means the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
something happening unexpectedly is out of its expected order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Politicians in a European assembly get an unexpected rush of adrenaline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges ADRENALINE, and 'surrounding' puts that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lower house of the Irish legislature, Ireland being a European country.

clue.text: Problems? Man's accommodating each involving father

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the man's letters hold the rest

parts.note: Man's is read as HE'S, with a man being he

indicators.note: involving here means taking in, so each wraps round the father

parts.note: each is taken as written
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A man houses each family member including father, and it causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Man's is read as HE'S without the apostrophe, and its letters split around the inner piece rather than staying together.
explanation.definitionFit: Headaches are troubles or nuisances, a figurative sense of the painful complaint.

clue.text: Instrument not entirely problematic with piano

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for problematic loses its final letter

parts.note: a hard task is a problematic one
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is a bit of a problem when paired with a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts HARD to HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp is a stringed musical instrument plucked by hand.

clue.text: Charge that could be arranged to harm Europe

indicators.note: letters that could be arranged are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: An accusation that might be arranged to damage Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation, but it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit measures electric charge: one ampere flowing for sixty minutes.

clue.text: Behind a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: The rear of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang this word means the buttocks, a person's backside.

clue.text: Verse mostly covering rise of Britain?

indicators.note: mostly means the word for covering loses its final letter

parts.note: a haik is an outer wrap worn in North Africa, a covering for head and body

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the letters are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: A poem mostly about Britain's ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: A haik is a North African cloak; 'mostly' trims it to HAI, and 'rise of' turns UK into KU.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of seventeen syllables, a form of verse.

clue.text: German missionary zeal not half is misdirected with wretch

indicators.note: something misdirected is sent the wrong way, so these letters go into a new order
not half means only one half of the word zeal is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A missionary's zeal is wasted on a wretched sinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves ZE from zeal; 'misdirected' rearranges ZE, IS and WRETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Schweitzer was a German-born medical missionary in Gabon and Nobel peace laureate.

clue.text: Drink taking large cut? One should keep locks in order

definitions.text: One should keep locks in order

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur
big means large
a rip is a tear or cut

explanation.surface: A drinker takes a big share; meanwhile someone keeps a door properly locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors, but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairgrip is a small sprung pin that holds hair neatly in place.

clue.text: Quiet about most of period backing metalworker

indicators.note: about means the quiet letters go around the rest

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: backing means the shortened period is read backwards
most of means the word for period loses its last letter

parts.note: a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: A craftsman stays quiet about time spent going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TIME to TIM; 'backing' makes MIT, which SH goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith forges metal, as in blacksmith or goldsmith.

clue.text: Head of mouse leading to startled cry? That's timid

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: eek is a cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A mouse pokes its head out and someone shrieks; that shows timidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek describes someone quiet and submissive, much like shy or timid.

clue.text: Crafty king stabbing expected nobleman

parts.note: arch means cunning or roguish

indicators.note: something stabbing goes into another thing, so the king goes inside expected

parts.note: due means expected
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A cunning king stabs a nobleman he was expecting to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An archduke is a high-ranking nobleman, especially in the Austrian imperial family.

clue.text: Drunken academic that is keeping lecturer in prominent position

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
prof is short for professor

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the lecturer goes within that is

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tipsy professor keeps a lecturer in a prominent post.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent and conspicuous is very visible to the public.

clue.text: Runner — hurt overcoming one on the terrible run

indicators.note: in a down clue overcoming means sitting over, placed above the next piece

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
A means one

indicators.note: terrible here means in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner, injured, beats someone on an awful run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ON THE into THONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathoner is a long-distance runner who takes part in marathons.

clue.text: A celebrant at work in place of worship

indicators.note: at work means being worked on, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A priest celebrating a service in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a sanctuary or meeting house used for religious services.

clue.text: Working at the farm may produce this

definitions.text: Working at the farm may produce this

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Farm work may produce a particular result.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal meaning is a second crop of grass after mowing, a real product of farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the second growth of grass after a mowing, so farm labour indeed yields it; figuratively it means consequences.

clue.text: Head of Greek army is an insubstantial figure

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude

explanation.surface: A Greek general turns out to be a mere shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit or spectre has no solid body, a figure without substance.

clue.text: Dishevelled attire one has to adjust

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone with messy clothes has to straighten themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to align or position correctly, which is to adjust or adapt.

clue.text: Entrances student to abandon a test

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave, so the student letter leaves the rest

parts.note: a trial is a test
L stands for a learner or student, as on learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student decides to skip an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' looks like a verb meaning enchants, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an entrance hall, and atria is its plural.

clue.text: English witticism is put into Old English for balance

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so is goes within Old English

explanation.surface: An English joke is translated into Old English for balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is equilibrium, an even balance of forces.

clue.text: Anglo-German humorist suspended, having penned dodgy number

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the suspended word holds the rest

parts.note: hung means suspended
off means bad or dodgy, as of food

explanation.surface: A comedian is suspended after writing a dodgy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerard Hoffnung was a German-born British cartoonist and musical humorist.

clue.text: I control game, upsetting Italian scientist

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means turning upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: I control the game is read as I'm ref, a referee being in charge

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be running the game while upsetting an Italian physicist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I control game' is I'M REF, which 'upsetting' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Fermi was an Italian physicist who built the first nuclear reactor.

clue.text: Half of publishers benefit

indicators.note: half of means only the second of the two founders' names in the publisher's title is kept

parts.note: Mills and ... is a British romance publisher named after its two founders

explanation.surface: Half the publishing houses gain something.
explanation.walkthrough: Mills & Boon is a famous British publisher of romantic fiction; 'Half of' keeps the second of its two founders' names.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing or advantage that someone gains is a benefit.

clue.text: River entering larger body of water, mostly for some entertainment

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the river goes into the shortened lake
mostly means the last letter of the larger body of water is dropped

parts.note: a lake is larger than a pond or river

explanation.surface: A river flows into a lake, mostly for people's enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a prank, some amusement.

clue.text: Sentence exemplified by preceding answer

definitions.meaning: a prison term; British slang from rhyming ... lime for time
the previous answer is a songbird, one example of the class

explanation.surface: A grammatical sentence illustrated by the last answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests grammar, but it is jail time in British slang (rhyming 'bird lime' with 'time'). The preceding answer, 24 Down, names a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing bird means serving a prison term, and the lark is one songbird.

clue.text: Sequence of monarchs dismissing a knight's standards

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the Normans were a line of English kings from William I
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A line of kings dismisses a knight for failing their standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are accepted standards or patterns of behaviour.

clue.text: Almost ready to pick up pouch

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the letters, reading them upward and so backwards
almost means the last letter of the word for ready is dropped

parts.note: ready money is cash

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly ready to collect a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims CASH to CAS; 'pick up' turns it to SAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a bag-like cavity in an animal or plant, a pouch.

clue.text: Opponent left off occupying rickety chair to make a racket

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the shortened opponent goes within the jumbled chair
rickety means shaky, so these letters are rearranged
off means taken away, so the left letter is removed

parts.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: An opponent leaves a wobbly chair, making a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left off' reads as a phrase meaning stopped, but 'left' gives L and 'off' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade, hence a cacophony or din.

clue.text: Spooner's destruction of links? Here's ticket for later event

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: a chain is made of links
a wreck is destruction

explanation.surface: A golf course is wrecked, so here is a ticket for a rescheduled event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' suggests a golf course, but means chain links; swapping the sounds of CHAIN WRECK gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a ticket for a rained-off baseball game, valid for a later game.

clue.text: Edit concluding section the writer's put in

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the writer goes within the concluding section

parts.note: the end is the concluding section
the writer refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: An editor tidies the final section the author has added.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or revise a text, as an editor does.
